Aggregation gives significant constant-factor savings over verifying signatures independently & \S{}2.2 & \textbf{Supported} & A/A-ind is ``net benefit'' by the \S{}6 rule in 16 of 16 warm cells and 16 of 16 cold cells. The ratio is 0.387--0.594 warm for N $\geq$ 2, and the saving grows with N rather than staying constant. \\
\addlinespace
Cost $\approx$ $\alpha$ + $\beta$N, with $\beta$ one hash to G2 plus one Miller loop per hop; which term dominates is left to measurement & \S{}4.6 & \textbf{Supported} & R\textsuperscript{2} 0.9994--0.9999 warm. $\beta$ = 189--211 \textmu{}s is 0.84--0.94 of hash + Miller loop (224 \textmu{}s). 10$\beta$/$\alpha$ = 3.417 [3.417, 3.418]: the per-hop term dominates by N = 10, from N $\approx$ 2.9. \\
\addlinespace
A chain carries a constant 96-byte signature regardless of N & \S{}2.2, \S{}4.3 & \textbf{Supported} & A's signature bytes are 96 at N = 1 and 96 at N = 10, in every profile. \\
\addlinespace
Carrying certificates inline costs more per hop than aggregation saves & \S{}8.2 & \textbf{Supported} & A certificate is 249 bytes (BLS) in this encoding; aggregation saves 98.0 bytes per hop over A-ind. Paper \S{}8.2's arithmetic assumes 48 + 96 bytes per certificate, which understates it. \\
\addlinespace
In the steady state, verification touches no registry & \S{}8.2 & \textbf{Supported} & Warm verifiers make no resolver or policy-store calls (\texttt{count-ops}: \texttt{tests/arms.rs} and \texttt{tests/security.rs::phase\_ordering\_count\_ops}). Cold N = 3 verifications make 4 + 1 calls (Q5). \\
\addlinespace
Cheap checks reject hostile chains before any pairing: \textbf{warm verifier} & \S{}4.6, Figure 2 & \textbf{Supported} & A warm verifier rejects line-34, expired and wrong-audience chains with no pairing (\texttt{tests/security.rs::phase\_ordering\_count\_ops}). \\
\addlinespace
Cheap checks reject hostile chains before any pairing: \textbf{cold verifier} & \S{}4.6, Figure 2 & \textbf{Not supported} & Line 24 verifies N + 1 certificates before phase 6, so a cold verifier pairs before rejecting a policy violation (P-28, D-61). Arm A costs 3573 \textmu{}s cold against 1144 \textmu{}s warm at N = 3. \\
